info.title: Ada Diamonds Agent API
info.summary: Read Ada Diamonds' lab grown diamond inventory, engagement ring settings, fine jewelry, and buying guides — and request a jeweler consultation.
info.description:
The Ada Diamonds Agent API gives AI agents and applications structured access to Ada Diamonds' live catalog and published content.

**Catalog and content endpoints require no credential.** An agent answering a shopper's question should not need an onboarding step first. Credentials exist to raise rate limits and to reach the endpoints that touch a specific customer's data. The API roots (`/api`, `/api/v1`) are the one read that challenges anonymous callers, with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header that points at the OAuth metadata.

**Pricing model.** An engagement ring is a setting plus a loose diamond, priced separately. `priceFrom` on a setting excludes the center stone. All prices are US dollars.

**Getting a credential.** `POST /api/v1/keys` issues a working API key immediately, no account required. For customer-specific access, register an OAuth client at `/api/oauth/register` and use the authorization code flow with PKCE.

**Sandbox.** Request `{"env":"sandbox"}` when creating a key. Sandbox credentials read the real catalog and accept writes without creating anything.

**Batching.** `POST /api/v1/batch` runs up to 20 public reads in one request and returns each sub-response with its own status. Use it to assemble a quote (a setting plus several stones) in a single round trip. A batch counts as one request against the rate limit.

**Long-running operations.** Whole-catalog exports are asynchronous: `POST /api/v1/exports` answers 202 with a `Location` header for the job. Poll `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` (honouring `Retry-After`) until `status` is `succeeded`, then download `result_url`. Exports complete within seconds and job ids stay valid for 24 hours. Operations marked `x-async: true` follow this pattern.

**MCP.** The same catalog is available as an MCP server at https://www.adadiamonds.com/mcp (streamable HTTP); the server card at https://www.adadiamonds.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json lists its tools.

servers.description: Sandbox: every path below, mounted under /sandbox. Credential-less requests are treated as the public sandbox key; reads return the live catalog, writes are acknowledged and create nothing. Described at /sandbox.

get.summary: API root: credential check and endpoint index
get.description: Returns a map of every endpoint with its operationId and auth requirement, plus the resolved credential (`anonymous` when the request carries none). No credential is needed: the roots are the first URLs an agent tries, and every catalog and content endpoint behind them is open. Protected endpoints answer 401 with a bare `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge whose `resource_metadata` parameter points at the OAuth protected-resource document.

get.summary: Versioned-root probe: the same endpoint index as /api/v1
get.description: Clients that guess `/v1` before reading any docs get the endpoint index, which says where the API is (`/api/v1`) and that it needs no account. The response is identical to `GET /api/v1`, credential resolution included; `/api/v1` remains the canonical root to link and cache.

Returns a page of Ada's live loose lab grown diamond inventory, filtered by shape, carat, price, color, clarity, and cut. Stones sell continuously, so treat results as a snapshot and call `getDiamond` to re-check a specific stone before quoting it. Prices are US dollars for the loose stone only; add a setting from `listEngagementRings` to quote a finished ring.

get.description: Returns a single loose diamond by its product id or by the grading report number (GCAL, IGI, or GIA), which is the identifier an agent usually has after reading a product page. A 404 means the stone has sold or the id is wrong; list current inventory with `listDiamonds` and pick again.

parameters.description: Product id (from `listDiamonds`) or grading report number.

Every setting is made to order in platinum or 14k/18k gold.

get.summary: Showroom locations and remote consultation options
get.description: Returns Ada's physical showroom(s) with address, hours, and phone, plus the virtual consultation details that serve shoppers everywhere else. Use it to answer whether someone outside New York can buy from Ada (yes, by video consultation) and where to book.

post.summary: Run several read requests in one call
post.description: Executes up to 20 GET requests against the public read endpoints in a single round trip and returns each sub-response with its own status and body. The batch always answers 200 once the envelope is valid, even if individual items fail, so check each item's `status`. Only the read endpoints listed in the `allowed_paths` of an error item can be batched; a batch counts as one request against the rate limit.

post.summary: Start a full catalog export (async job)
post.description: Starts an export of the diamonds, engagement ring, or jewelry catalog with the same filters the list endpoint accepts, and answers **202 Accepted** with a `Location` header pointing at the job's status URL. Exports complete within seconds: poll `status_url` (honouring `Retry-After`) until `status` is `succeeded`, then download `result_url`. Job ids are self-contained signed tokens valid for 24 hours; there is nothing to cancel.

202.description: The export job was accepted. Poll the `Location` URL.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the first poll (2).

get.description: Streams the export as `application/x-ndjson` (one product per line, default) or as a JSON array, depending on the `format` chosen when the job was created. Rows have exactly the field shape of the matching list endpoint, with prices in US dollars. The response is an attachment (`Content-Disposition`) and is never cached.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id returned by `createExport`.

X-Export-Count.description: Number of rows in the export.

schema.description: One JSON object per line; each is a Diamond, EngagementRing, or JewelryItem.

get.summary: Get the status of an async job
get.description: Reports the state of a job started by `createExport`. A job is `queued` for a moment after creation (the response carries `Retry-After`) and `succeeded` after that, at which point `result_url` is set. Expired jobs (older than 24 hours) return 410; start a new export.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id returned by `createExport`.

Retry-After.description: Present while the job is still `queued`: seconds to wait before polling again.

post.description: Creates a real consultation request that a jeweler answers by email within one business day. Requires the `appointments:write` scope, which is only issued through the authorization code flow, so the customer has approved the request. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried request cannot create a duplicate lead; sandbox credentials get a 201 without creating anything.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when this is the stored response to an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

409.description: A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still in flight. Retry shortly.

422.description: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used with a different request body. Use a new key.

post.description: Returns a working API key immediately, with no account and no human approval. Keys are limited to the public read scopes and mainly buy a higher rate limit; the key is shown once and stored only as a hash, so save it. Request `env: "sandbox"` to get a key whose writes are acknowledged and discarded.

201.description: The key. Store it now; it is not retrievable.

get.description: A short JSON description of the registration endpoint: what to POST, the defaults, and the related OAuth client registration endpoint. Read it once if the 201 body of the POST is not self-explanatory; nothing is created by a GET.

post.summary: Register an agent: a sandbox API key with no body required
post.description: Zero-friction registration. POST with an empty body, plain text, a form, or the same JSON as `/api/v1/keys` and get a working key back at once: no account, no email, no approval. `name` defaults to `self-serve agent key` and `env` to `sandbox`; send `env: "production"` for a production key with the same public read scopes. A body shaped like RFC 7591 client metadata (`redirect_uris`, `client_name`) is treated as OAuth dynamic client registration instead. Also served at `/register`, `/signup`, and `/api/agents/register`.

201.description: The key. Store it now; it is not retrievable.

post.description: Identical to `POST /api/register`: an empty body returns a sandbox API key at once. Kept because some clients try this path first; `/register` and `/signup` are the same door.

201.description: The key. Store it now; it is not retrievable.

get.description: The single free developer tier (rate limits, scopes, sandbox) and how products are priced (setting plus loose diamond, US dollars), with live price bands from the catalog feeds.

get.summary: Structured agent view of the site
get.description: Any page URL with `?mode=agent` returns interfaces, authentication, capabilities, content indexes, rate limits, and contact as a linked HTML page. Send `Accept: application/json` for JSON or `Accept: text/markdown` for markdown.
A scoped llms.txt for one section of the site. Served at /developers/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /docs/llms.txt, /knowledge-base/llms.txt, /mcp/llms.txt, and /developers/commerce/llms.txt.
NLWeb 0.55 endpoint over the live catalog, the knowledge base, and the developer docs. Also served at https://www.adadiamonds.com/ask. Send `Accept: text/event-stream` or `streaming=true` for SSE.

post.description: Assemble a cart from product-feed item ids (`diamond:<report number>`, `setting:<slug>`, `jewelry:<slug>`) and get back a Stripe-hosted checkout URL the buyer opens to pay; no card data passes through the agent. Requires the shipping address (tax and shipping are priced into the link); buyer email is optional and collected on the payment page when missing. Anonymous callers are allowed, and an anonymous or production-credential request without `env: "sandbox"` creates a LIVE, payable Stripe Checkout session; a sandbox credential or `env: "sandbox"` returns a simulated link and creates no Stripe session. (The MCP `create_checkout_link` tool differs: anonymous MCP calls default to sandbox and need `env: "production"` for a live link.) Links expire after 24 hours. On payment, the order flows through the standard pipeline (order confirmation email, jeweler follow-up on size and metal).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional but recommended on state-changing requests; a reused key with a different body is rejected with 409.

parameters.name: Request-Id
parameters.description: Trace id; echoed back when provided.

200.description: The cart needs more input; `problems[]` lists what is missing and `url` is null.

201.description: A payable link was created; `url` is the Stripe-hosted checkout page.

400.description: Malformed body, unknown item id, or an unavailable product.

post.description: Create a session from product-feed item ids (`diamond:<id>`, `setting:<slug>`, `jewelry:<slug>`). Returns a priced session; add buyer and shipping address to reach `ready_for_payment`. Sandbox credentials (including the public key `ada_test_public_sandbox_key`) create sandbox sessions that never charge.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required on every POST. Opaque string up to 255 characters (UUID v4 recommended), scoped to the credential and endpoint; the same key with a different body is rejected.

get.description: Return the latest state of a checkout session inside the `ucp` negotiation envelope. Status uses the UCP vocabulary (`incomplete`, `ready_for_complete`, `complete_in_progress`, `completed`, `canceled`) and amounts are integer cents in USD. An unknown id, or one owned by another credential, is a business outcome: HTTP 200 with `ucp.status: error` and a `not_found` message. Requires a bearer token; the sandbox key returns sandbox sessions.

IdempotencyKey.description: A client-generated unique key making this request safe to retry. This endpoint creates a Salesforce Lead, so a retry without a key can create a duplicate. Replaying a key with the same body returns the original response with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reusing it with a different body returns 422. Keys are honoured for 24 hours.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed. `error_description` says which field.

Unauthorized.description: A credential is required. The `WWW-Authenticate` header carries the RFC 9728 `resource_metadata` pointer; follow it to the authorization server, or send a self-serve API key.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bare RFC 6750 challenge: `Bearer realm="Ada Diamonds API", resource_metadata="https://www.adadiamonds.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`.

Forbidden.description: The credential is valid but lacks the required scope, or the scope cannot be self-issued.

NotFound.description: Nothing at that id. `error_description` says where to list what exists.

Gone.description: The job expired (24 hours). Start a new export.

InvalidJobToken.description: The job id's signature does not verify. Use ids exactly as issued.

RateLimited.description: Over the rate limit. Wait `Retry-After` seconds; a credential raises the limit.

RateLimit.description: RFC 9331 combined budget, e.g. `limit=120, remaining=118, reset=42`. Read it to pace yourself.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

X-API-Version.description: The API version that served the response.

UpstreamUnavailable.description: A catalog or content feed is temporarily unavailable. Retry in a few seconds.
